title: Adults More Creative than Kids, Less Confident — Study
paragraphs: Many people believe that young children are more creative than adults. However, a recent study has found that it's adults who may actually be more creative — they're just less confident!

The study was published in PLOS One, and included 92 preschool children and 70 adults, with 85% of the adults aged between 20 and 30 years old. Each participant took part in the same three creative activities.
First, everyone was given a tin can and three minutes to think of how many ways they could use it.

Next, they all spent eight minutes drawing whatever they wanted with colored pens. The researchers chose to make this part seem like it wasn't a test, and just a chance for participants to get used to the materials for the next part.
Finally, everyone used those same materials to spend another eight minutes inventing and drawing their own unique fantasy animal.
After these three tasks, the participants answered questions about how confident or anxious they felt, and how much they enjoyed the activities.

Trained judges then looked at the products from each task, from tin can ideas to fantasy masterpieces. They actually found that adults' ideas were more original, effective and creative than what the children came up with.
The preschool children felt much better about their efforts, though — they enjoyed the tasks more, were more motivated and less anxious about their work than the adults.

Also, when asked, more than three-quarters of the adults in the study believed that the children were more creative than them. The researchers think this may be because adults see children's enthusiasm and confidence as proof of their greater creativity.

The study also found that children take part in creative activities far more often than adults — an average of once a day versus once a week — which again could cause grown-ups to see children as more creative.
